newsitem.title: USA: Coleman sees small Q3 loss.
newsitem.headline: Coleman sees small Q3 loss.

text.p: The Coleman Company said Thursday that sales of its camping related recreation products in North America and Japan experienced softness in the third quarter ending September 30.
Combined with the expected first year dilutive effect of its recent European acquisition, Camping Gaz, the company said it will report a small loss in the third quarter.
In the comparable period of 1995, Coleman said it earned 17 cents per share before an extraordinary item.
Coleman said it expects to resume normal earnings in the fourth quarter, excluding the expected dilutive effect of Camping Gaz, which will cause a small reported loss.
The company also said it will take one time, after tax, charges in the third and fourth quarters totaling about $50 million.

The company said the bulk of the charges relate to restructuring its worldwide recreation business, reflecting the integration of Camping Gaz, and the withdrawal from the entry level electric pressure washer market.

Coleman said it has found greater than previously identified cost savings as it integrates Camping Gaz into its nearly $1 billion global recreation business. These savings of about $20 million annually will phase in during 1997 and enable a cut in the company's global recreation work force of over 10 percent, the company said.

The company said that despite withdrawing from entry level electric pressure washer market, it will continue to market gas powered units, a category in which it has a substantial and growing market share.
